stemMd: According to the passage, what can time diaries reveal that questionnaires cannot?

options.label: A
options.textMd: How people's schedules change from one week to the next.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Which occupations have the longest working weeks.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Which activities were carried out at the same time.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Whether respondents are deliberately misreporting their hours.

options.label: E
options.textMd: How many hours of paid work people do in a typical week.

explanationMd:
Find the sentence that answers the question and read it exactly. In the second paragraph: "Diaries also reveal something questionnaires cannot: which activities were carried out at the same time." The example of the parent cooking, listening to a child read and answering a message illustrates it.

The wrong choices can be checked against the text. Hours of paid work are reported by both instruments, which the passage says give different figures, so they are not something only diaries reveal. Dishonesty is discussed in the first paragraph and dismissed as the usual cause of the gap. Schedule variation is what a one-day diary is *bad* at capturing. Occupations are never mentioned.

distractorRationale.e: Questionnaires also report weekly hours of paid work; the passage says the two instruments give different figures for it, not that only diaries can produce one.
distractorRationale.d: The first paragraph says the gap between reported and recorded hours is not usually dishonesty, and no instrument is said to reveal intent.
distractorRationale.a: The third paragraph says the opposite: a single day says little about someone whose schedule varies from week to week.
distractorRationale.b: The passage does not compare occupations.

accessibilityText: A stated-information question about the time diaries passage. It asks what time diaries can reveal that questionnaires cannot. The five choices: how people's schedules change from one week to the next; which occupations have the longest working weeks; which activities were carried out at the same time; whether respondents are deliberately misreporting their hours; how many hours of paid work people do in a typical week.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage. Every option is answerable, or refutable, from the passage text alone.

review.author: tolc-e-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The passage states it directly: 'Diaries also reveal something questionnaires cannot: which activities were carried out at the same time.' A is named as a weakness of diaries (one day says little about variable schedules). E is something both instruments measure, and diaries cover only one or two days. B and D are not stated, and D is weakened by 'not usually dishonesty'. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-verbal-run2) reached the same answer: The passage states it directly: 'Diaries also reveal something questionnaires cannot: which activities were carried out at the same time.' A is contradicted, because a single diary day 'says little' about schedules that change. B and D are not in the passage. E is something both instruments measure, so it isn't unique to diaries.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: the second paragraph states the answer in one sentence; each other choice is contradicted or absent. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
